title: Acme Corp — pricing pushback
description: Discovery call where the prospect likes the product but stalls on annual pricing and asks for a pilot.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Thanks for jumping on, Priya. I saw you evaluated three tools last quarter — what's still open?

transcript.speaker: Prospect
transcript.text: We need deal notes that our AEs actually trust. Gong is too expensive for a twelve-person team.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Got it. OpenGong Lite gives you objections, next steps, and receipts back to the transcript — no seat tax.

transcript.speaker: Prospect
transcript.text: That sounds right. My worry is accuracy. If a claim isn't in the call, our CRM gets polluted.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Every claim has to point to an exact line. Unproven claims never ship — that's a hard gate.

transcript.speaker: Prospect
transcript.text: Okay, but annual pricing is still a stretch. Can we do a thirty-day pilot on two teams first?

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Yes. We can start a pilot next Monday with your enterprise and mid-market pods.

transcript.speaker: Prospect
transcript.text: If the pilot proves out, I'll bring procurement in the week after. Intent is to replace Fireflies by Q3.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll send a follow-up with the pilot plan, success metrics, and a draft SOW outline.

transcript.speaker: Prospect
transcript.text: Send it today so I can share with our RevOps lead before Friday's forecast meeting.

followUpEmail.body:
Priya —

Great conversation. Attaching the pilot plan, success metrics, and a draft SOW outline.

Proposed start: next Monday with your enterprise and mid-market pods for 30 days.

Success bar: AE-trusted notes with transcript receipts (no unproven CRM claims).

Please share with RevOps ahead of Friday's forecast meeting. If the pilot proves out, we can loop procurement the week after.

— OpenGong Lite
